body:
Ares is enacting its lowest level of private credit deals in five years as it envisions “cracks appearing” in the space.

Speaking at the Citi Investment Conference in Sydney on 20 October, Peter Graf, partner and head of Asia direct lending at Ares Credit Group, said he is “cautiously optimistic” about the sector but that the firm is being especially selective right now.

“We are cautiously optimistic, Australia is better placed than the rest of the world and our portfolios are holding up pretty well. But if inflation and rates stay high for an extended period of time, if you have pressure on input costs…. I would say our underwriting standards are higher today than they were six months ago.”

This means the number of deals the firm is enacting is at its lowest level in five years, he said.

“Noone is saying the sky is falling but we are trying to be cautious, you will see more and more cracks appearing so partnering with the right manager and right asset strategy is crucial.”

Also appearing on the panel, Mark Glengarry, senior managing director and head of APAC at Blackstone Credit and Insurance, agreed there was the potential for problems in the space but optimistically said this could highlight different skillsets.

“We do see dispersion and some industries are under pressure but there is a lot more resilience in the global economy than people think and not every business was impacted in the same way.

“What you see now [in Australia] is an evolution and a focus on underlying companies, having the right skillset within the management team and a real strategy in place. It is not just about minimising losses but also maximising return.

“You see a more sophisticated dialogue when companies are in difficulty, it becomes about how do you deliver value and drive performance? How do you keep driving forward?”

The pair also briefly touched on the collapse of Bathla, the Western Sydney property developer which collapsed into administration on 25 August owing $3 billion.

Since then, residential property and private credit have seen increased security as several funds including Centuria Bass’ Bass Credit Fund and Bass Property Credit Fund temporarily paused redemptions over exposure concerns.

Graf said: “Bathla is complicated structure with a number of different assets and lenders, my guess from reading the press is a number of those lenders will be OK if they have done the right due diligence on the assets they underwrote.”

Returning to his theme of cracks in the sector, he added: “Real estate has been a huge focus of growth in private credit over the last 5-10 years and the information you get from each manager needs to be looked at closely. There will be cracks or stresses coming through more as interest rates rise, that’s tough on real estate. You’ve got to watch closely what you are underwriting, how the businesses are going and how you end up working with those parties.”
